title: Quantization runtime instability impacting RLHF long-context models — root cause and mitigation plan
creator: Elena Garcia
description: High-severity incident: a new dynamic per-layer quantization estimator deployed to serving caused instability for a subset of RLHF conversational models with long contexts. The behavior manifested as token corruption and crash loops under high concurrency, plus subtle accuracy drift for long-turn dialogues. The autotuner change was rolled back and a multi-part remediation plan has been completed.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-11 a runtime change that adjusted per-layer scale heuristics for int8 serving produced incorrect dequantization for certain attention head layouts when combined with the KV-cache offset optimization. This caused requests to either return garbled tokens (accuracy regression) or trigger runtime exceptions leading to crash loops on some GPU workers. The issue affected hosted API customers during regional scale events and several Dedicated pools running long-context RLHF models.
timeline: 2026-03-11 02:12 UTC — Canary deploy of quant-estimator v2.3 started in region eu-west-1
2026-03-11 02:45 UTC — Error spike detected: token corruption and out-of-bounds kernel exceptions on 6% of requests (Grafana alert #Q-9472)
2026-03-11 03:05 UTC — Automated canary rollback failed for one pool; manual rollback initiated
2026-03-11 03:20 UTC — Full rollback of quant-estimator v2.3 completed; errors dropped to baseline
2026-03-11 04:00 UTC — Post-rollback validation run on replay dataset confirmed reduced crash rate but showed lingering accuracy drift for 3 RLHF model variants
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC — Incident declared P0; on-call, runtime, and model teams paged
2026-03-11 13:00 UTC — Hotfix branch created to add strict dequant validation and per-model fallback to FP16; hotfix landed and rolled to affected pools by 2026-03-12
root_cause: A change in the dynamic per-layer scale estimator produced scale factors that, when combined with an existing KV-cache byte-offset optimization, resulted in mismatched dequantization ordering for certain attention head packing layouts. The runtime's assumption about scale/zero-point ordering did not hold for a small subset of model shims used by RLHF pipelines. Under high concurrency the mismatch led to out-of-bounds memory accesses in the int8 dequant kernel and nondeterministic token corruption in surviving requests.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back quant-estimator v2.3 across all regions — removed the new heuristic
Applied hotfix to runtime to add explicit dequant ordering checks and safe-fallthrough to FP16 on mismatch
Enabled model-level feature flag to force FP16 for known-affected RLHF variants during peak windows
Increased canary window and added synthetic long-context workloads to canary traffic
long_term_actions: ENG-18305: Add low-level dequant ordering unit tests and fuzz harness for attention packing (owner: Priya Reddy, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-18312: Expand canary gating to include long-context RLHF replay datasets and include deployment block on replay mismatch >0.2% (owner: Omar Diaz, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-18320: Implement automated model-level fallback and rollback automation so Dedicated pools can opt into safe variants without manual intervention (owner: Rajat Mehra, due: 2026-04-08)
ENG-18330: Post-deploy telemetry metric: per-model dequant-mismatch-rate and kernel-exception-rate with alerting (owner: Elena Garcia, due: 2026-03-29)
ENG-18355: Add regression test in CI against public RLHF reference workloads and include long-turn conversational traces (owner: Sato Nakamura, due: 2026-04-12)
follow_up_notes: Canary sizing underestimated long-context variance — update canary runner to synthesize longer sequence distributions
Autotuner team to add conservative fallback when scale estimates are low confidence
Dedicated customers impacted were offered a status summary and the option to pin runtime-1.21 for 30 days; two customers accepted
We observed no indicators of data leakage or security compromise during the incident
customer_communications: 2026-03-11 16:30 UTC — Initial incident notification sent to affected Dedicated customers
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC — Follow-up with technical summary and mitigation steps; offered rollback/pinning option

closure_notes: Incident resolved with rollback and runtime hotfix. Primary engineering remediations are in flight; canary and CI changes must land before we resume aggressive autotuner releases. Postmortem reviewed with PM, Model Ops, and Customers Team on 2026-03-12. Action items assigned and tracked under ENG-183xx series.
